title: On conditional parity as a notion of non-discrimination in machine learning
findings: The paper uses a hypothetical scenario of a church hiring a priest to illustrate the difference between counterfactual fairness (CF) and equalized counterfactual odds (ECO). It finds that in this scenario, a hiring process that favors a Christian applicant over an equally qualified atheist applicant would not be counterfactually fair, but would satisfy ECO. This example serves to highlight the nuances and stringency of different fairness definitions.
